findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn't an employee who was food manager certified on the premise. Shortly throughout the inspection, the only employee who is food manager certified arrived. Discussed the need to have at least two employees who are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation. Ensure that a CFPM is present if open for operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A significant amount of mold was observed on a container of cooked chili within the line prep cooler along the cookline. Date marking was also lacking for this food item. Shown to the PIC and the chili was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that preparation/discard dates are checked daily to be sure that foods are getting rotated correctly and pulled before they get the chance to spoil or go bad.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of ground beef stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods inside a prep cooler along the cook-line. Shown the PIC and the ground beef was moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal proteins are always stored beneath RTE foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were many Time/Temperature Control foods that lacked date marking in the prep coolers along the cook-line. The foods include cheeses, sauces, chili, and cooked noodles. The foods were shown to the PIC and were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are never stored in house longer than seven days after they are opened or prepared.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The bottom surfaces, as well as the shelving inside all prep coolers along the cook-line were observed with accumulated food debris. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that inner surfaces of prep coolers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cooled chili in the prep cooler to lack date marking. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the item was prepared yesterday and placed the correct corresponding date on the food. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with the day of preparation/ thawing/ opening to be used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
The facility did not have an allergen awareness sign posted. CORRECTED- a sign was placed on the left side of the ordering window. Ensure allergen awareness signage is always visible to the consumer when ordering.

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple white powders throughout the facility (one on the cook-line, and 2 in dry storage) with no label. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed a label on the items. Ensure items that may easily confused with others are labeled once removed from their original packaging to prevent the risk of contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FOURTH REPEAT: The restroom door is not self-closing. A restroom without a self-closer poses a risk of contamination of food products.  Add a self-closer to the restroom door.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
5th REPEAT: Mop sink room is mostly unfinished. The following repairs/maintenance activities are needed in the mop room:
-Surfaces surrounding the sink should be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable. See that the wall to floor is covered/baseboard.
-See that walls are smooth and painted with a semi-gloss paint.
-Caulk sink to wall.
-Ceiling should be smooth and easily cleanable at least over the mop sink area.

A discussion regarding planned reconstruction took place between the inspector and the PIC. PIC stated that the facility has recently merged ownership with their building-mates. Both PICs are balancing assets. A quote for construction has been placed on the room. Further communication will occur between the operator and SCDPH regarding the reconstruction.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: 4th REPEAT: Trim tiles along the wall under the 3 compartment sink and dish machine are not sealed to the wall, creating a gap between the tile and the wall. Openings between the floor and wall can allow for the harborage of mold. Seal the wall to floor and eliminate the gap.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The Food Handler Certificate of one of the kitchen staff was observed to have expired in 2024. PIC is aware of the lapse in certification and has posted a list of companies by which the staff member may renew their certificate. Ensure all staff members have an active Food Handlers card by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Thawed ROP fish was observed still sealed in its packaging that bore a label indicating the need to remove from packaging prior to thawing. CORRECTED- PIC cut the packages open. Ensure ROP fish packages are cut prior to thawing to introduce oxygen and prevent botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The small freezer on the cookline was observed with frost accumulation on interior surfaces. Defrost the freezer regularly to prevent frost accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.comment:
-1st REPEAT: Raw shell eggs were observed stored above whole bell peppers and next to whole onions in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged so that eggs were not above vegetables or potentially ready-to-eat foods. Review storage order to prevent cross contamination.
-Raw meat observed stored above cheese in the bottom of the short prep cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged and cheese was voluntarily discarded.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition

3rd REPEAT: Foods observed in the under counter cooler and in the 2 door cooler more than 7 days past their prep/open dates. Foods observed include pizza sauce (dated 9/1), tomato paste (dated 9-8), and hush puppy batter (dated 8/27). Foods 7 days or more past their prep/open dates were voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Employee observed placing a bun on the grill then plating the same bun with bare hands. CORRECTED- Discussed using clean gloved hands or utensils to handle ready-to-eat foods with PIC and employee.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs were observed stored above sliced cheeses and whole potatoes in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged so that eggs were not above vegetables or potentially ready-to-eat foods. Review storage order to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
A pan of nacho cheese was observed in the drawer cooler at 53F (probed). Per PIC, the cheese was made yesterday (label read 4/12, tomorrow). CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling timeline. Monitor cooling temperatures to ensure benchmarks are reached.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Foods observed in prep coolers and under counter cooler more than 7 days past their prep/open dates. Foods observed include pork gravy (dated 3/12) and confi (dated 3/1). Foods 7 days or more past their prep/open dates were voluntarily discarded. (This violation was previously observed during the 10/12/23 and 5/24/23 routine inspections.)
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Foods observed in the prep coolers and under counter cooler without date markings. Foods observed include rice/orzo, egg rolls, and several sauces. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the egg rolls with the date the pork filling was cooked. Other foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods are labeled with the date they are prepared/opened. (This violation was previously observed at the 10/12/23 and 5/24/23 inspections.)
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (F) Does not apply to shellstock. (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Cooling methods used were inadequate to cool nacho cheese sauce to 41F or below in 6 hours or less. CORRECTED- Discussed cooling methods, such as shallow pans and ice baths. The drawer cooler and prep coolers are likely not designed to cool foods from hot temperatures. Review cooling methods with staff and ensure effective methods are used.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [Pf]
